territorial_scope.description: Applies to processing of personal data of data subjects in Nigeria, including by controllers or processors not domiciled in Nigeria who process or target such data.

evidence.quote: applies to a data controller or data processor not domiciled in Nigeria but processes the personal data of a data subject in Nigeria

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Binding implementing directive of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission under the NDP Act 2023. Sets controller and processor duties (registration and audits for major data processors, DPOs, lawful bases, consent, DPIAs, 72-hour breach notice, data subject rights) and cross-border transfer rules, applying from issuance, including safeguards for AI and other emerging technologies.
summary.long: The General Application and Implementation Directive (GAID) 2025 of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission issues binding guidance under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. From its issuance, the NDPR 2019 ceases to apply as a legal instrument for data privacy (Art. 3(3)). It covers processing of personal data of data subjects in Nigeria, including by controllers not domiciled there (Art. 1). Main provisions: compliance measures for controllers and processors (Art. 7); designation of major-importance controllers and processors in UHL, EHL and OHL tiers, with registration and annual compliance audit returns (Arts. 8-10, Schedule 7); DPO designation and duties (Arts. 11-14); principles and lawful bases, including consent and cookie consent (Arts. 15-26); information to data subjects (Art. 27); mandatory DPIAs in listed circumstances (Art. 28); security schedules and 72-hour breach notification (Arts. 29, 33); processing agreements (Art. 34); data subject rights (Arts. 36-38); complaints and investigations (Art. 39); ethics, and emerging technologies including AI (Arts. 41-44); cross-border transfers (Art. 45, Schedule 5); capacity building (Art. 46); and fees and filing charges (Schedules 7, 10). Exemptions and legal-obligation grounds are addressed in Arts. 5 and 22. Enforcement includes Commission remedial directions and temporary orders (Art. 39(12)-(13)) and an administrative penalty of 50% of the filing fee for late filing (Art. 10(9)).

notes: Target instrument IDs, LEI and ticker are left empty (not resolved against the registry). Text-internal issues: Schedule 7 heading cites 'Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2003' while the Act is 2023; Schedule 7 para 3(1)(d) and (f) cross-refer to 3(1)(e) and 3(1)(g), which do not match the categories intended; Schedule 10 EHL band B reads '5,000-2,500'; Schedule 7 is dated 19 December 2024 while Schedule 10 is issued 20 March 2025 and the cover says 2025. Article 3(2) says the NDP Act prevails over the GAID in a conflict. Only relations and entities were annotated in this pass; obligations, thresholds, events and other sections were outside the requested fields.

definitions.term: data controller or data processor of major importance
definitions.defined_in: NDP Act 2023 s.65 (quoted in GAID Art. 8(1))

evidence.quote: “data controller or data processor of major importance” means a data controller or data processor that is domiciled, resident in, or operating in Nigeria

definitions.defined_in: NDP Act 2023 s.65 (interpreted in GAID Art. 8(2))

evidence.quote: “Operating in Nigeria” as stated in section 65 includes a data controller or a data processor who targets a data subject in Nigeria.
“domiciliation” means the state of living or permanently residing in a place.
Ultra-High Level (UHL) shall be a category of data controllers and data processors of major importance
Extra-High Level (EHL) shall be a category of data controllers and data processors of major importance
Ordinary-High Level (MDP-OHL) shall be a category of data controllers and data processors of major importance
“data protection officer” is an expert in data protection law and practices.
“duly certified” means certified by an institution that is accredited or approved by a competent authority in data privacy protection or in educational services.
“disparate outcome or disparate impact” means an adverse effect of carrying out an appropriate task.
“interoperable data privacy measures” are essentially tools and approaches that ensure different data protection laws and frameworks work together seamlessly.
“platform of data processing” means any medium through which a data controller or a data processor handles personal data.
“regulatory instruments” mean laws, regulations, directives, codes, guidelines and guidance notices and certifications.

definitions.term: may (in the context of an obligation in this GAID)

evidence.quote: “may” when used in the context of an obligation in this GAID, indicates that there exist accountability safeguards for regulatory actions for data controllers or data processors to take into consideration.
The items listed in sub (3) above are hereafter referred to collectively as Special Rule of Law Indexes (SRLI).
A data subject’s vulnerability index is a risk factor which may be peculiar to a data subject, a group or a class of data subject
